data.narrative:
General Matter is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Scott Nolan and Lee Robinson, having raised $50M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 nuclear energy firms—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo—spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $50M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implies a $100M valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comps—Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A)—yields a median of $808M, with a range of $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects stage and technology heterogeneity within nuclear energy infrastructure.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $85M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $454M. Material uncertainties include the discrete stage gaps and divergent maturity profiles among peers, particularly between seed-stage and Series B positions. The peer-median result carries elevated variance given the small sample and the wide valuation spread in early-stage nuclear, warranting downward pressure toward the $200M–$450M band absent material technical or commercial differentiation data.
